translations.translatedText: # Tuesday 5.7.2022
NATO observer membership. Accession talks. Nurse shortage. Restaurant tax evasion. Weather forecast.
The TV's Clear News has a summer break from 6.6. to 12.8.
Read and listen to the radio broadcast here.
## Finland's NATO membership

![Pekka Haavisto, Jens Stoltenberg and Magdalena Andersson stand behind speaker's podiums.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5120,h_2880,x_0,y_453/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-97818862c40a733341c/1657016017)
Open image viewer
Finnish Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto, NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg and Swedish Foreign Minister Ann Linde at the signing ceremony in Brussels. Photo: Kenzo Tribouillard / AFP
Finland and Sweden have been accepted as NATO observer members. Finland and Sweden signed the accession protocols to NATO in Brussels on Tuesday.

Finland and Sweden can now take part in NATO meetings, but they cannot yet vote in NATO meetings. Full NATO membership requires that all 30 NATO member countries approve Finland's and Sweden's membership.
Many countries have promised to approve the membership quickly. In some countries handling the matter may take several months.
## NATO talks
![Pekka Haavisto at a press briefing.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5120,h_2880,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-97822362c41558e2e2e/1657017736)
Open image viewer
Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto says the talks progressed quickly. Photo: Kenzo Tribouillard / AFP
Finland's talks on joining NATO progressed quickly on Tuesday. Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto says that 4 hours had been reserved for the accession talks, but the accession talks took only 2 hours.

NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg is pleased that Finland and Sweden are joining the defence alliance NATO. Stoltenberg is also glad that Finland and Sweden have reached an agreement with Turkey.
Turkey at first opposed Finland's and Sweden's NATO membership, but stopped opposing it after negotiations.
## Nurse shortage

![Donna Cosio, working as a care assistant at Attendo Vanamo care home in Kemijärvi, stands in the common room of the care home with a landscape wall behind her.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5548,h_3120,x_0,y_269/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-97603962bc4dae658cd/1656507915)
Open image viewer
Donna Cosio came to Finland from the Philippines. She cares for elderly people in Kemijärvi. Photo: Elina Ervasti / Yle

There is a severe shortage of nurses in Finland. The new nurse staffing ratio also increases the need for nurses in hospitals and care homes. That is why more nurses are being recruited to Finland from abroad than before.

For example, the health sector temporary employment company Mehiläinen HSS brings about 500 care assistants to Finland this year and about 1000 care assistants next year. The temporary employment company Barona brings 500 nurses to Finland this year.
Nurses are being hired to Finland from far away, for example from the Philippines and India.
## Restaurant tax evasion
![Open cash register.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/17-63453392b6ecb7a3/1396859430)
Open image viewer
The Tax Administration recommends that people do not pay in cash at restaurants. Photo: YLE
The Tax Administration has found a lot of tax evasion in the restaurant industry. Inspections showed that almost 20 million euros of taxes have remained unpaid in the restaurant industry since 2017.
Of that sum, 8 million euros is unpaid corporate income tax. The Tax Administration found a total of 40 million euros of income that had been hidden from the Tax Administration.
The Tax Administration recommends that people do not pay in cash at a restaurant. It is good to check that the receipt has all the products the customer has bought from the restaurant marked on it.
